name: Meropenem
high_alert_note: Not confirmed as high-alert on a source read; the institution's list governs.
summary: Penem antibacterial for infections including complicated skin and skin-structure infections. Nursing focus: hypersensitivity, severe skin reactions, seizures and the interaction with valproic acid.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

items.text: The label describes meropenem as a penem antibacterial indicated for the treatment of several infections, including complicated skin and skin-structure infections.
Ask about previous reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics and about valproic acid or divalproex use, and report both.
Monitoring frequency and alarm limits follow the unit's protocol for this medicine.

The label describes seizures and other CNS adverse experiences, severe cutaneous adverse reactions (such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis), and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhoea (ranging from mild to fatal colitis) as reasons to watch for and evaluate new neurological symptoms, skin changes, or diarrhoea; it also notes thrombocytopenia has been observed in patients with renal dysfunction, and warns that giving meropenem with valproic acid or divalproex reduces valproic acid levels, which can increase the risk of breakthrough seizures.
Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions have been reported with beta-lactams.
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions have been reported.
Seizures and other central nervous system adverse experiences have been reported.
Co-administration with valproic acid or divalproex sodium reduces serum valproic acid concentrations, potentially increasing the risk of breakthrough seizures.
Rhabdomyolysis and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhoea (mild to fatal) are listed among the warnings.
The label lists hypersensitivity reactions and severe cutaneous reactions among the adverse reactions discussed in its warnings.
Stop and call for help for allergic signs or a seizure; report persistent diarrhoea and rash.
Record the product and order checks, monitoring results, adverse events and escalation per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Check allergy history and any valproate medicine.
Watch for rash, breathing difficulty and seizures.
Monitor stool frequency and report persistent diarrhoea.
Report allergy, seizure or severe diarrhoea at once.
